PullRequest.Title: Show a language-status warning for diagnostic highlight limits

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed limit and call path are explicit: `MarkerService.onMarkerChanged` reaches `_updateDecorations`, `update` allocates Sets over the full capped collection and `deltaDecorations` synchronously creates interval nodes. The PR body also measures `_updateDecorations` rising from 11.34 ms to 29.01 ms normally and from 21.20 ms to 70.01 ms under 4x throttling. Only trigger prevalence is uncertain; the supplied multi-provider example establishes a realistic way to exceed 500.
Findings.PerformanceResource: model decoration objects, interval-tree nodes, Set allocations, and UI-thread CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Per affected model and marker update, comparison and creation scale with the capped diagnostic count, increased from O(min(n, 500)) to O(min(n, 5000)); retained decoration state likewise increases by up to 4,500 objects/nodes per loaded model.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased synchronous latency and dropped frames, plus higher retained memory and GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The service read and decorated only the first 500 diagnostics per loaded model, bounding synchronous diff/insertion work and retained decoration state at 500.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Marker changes and model creation now eagerly materialize, interval-tree insert, retain, and compare as many as 5,000 marker decorations per loaded model rather than 500.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 147 introduces `MAX_MARKER_DECORATIONS_LIMIT = 5000`, and RIGHT line 122 uses that value to read and pass up to 5,000 markers into `MarkerDecorations.update`; the deleted implementation read only 500.
Findings.Title: Keep the default diagnostic decoration cap at 500
Findings.Impact: A large/generated file receiving diagnostics from several providers can block the editor UI for multiple frames whenever diagnostics are initially published or republished, with additional CPU/GC pressure and up to ten times as many retained decoration nodes even for non-visible loaded models.
Findings.Evidence: `MarkerDecorationsService` subscribes globally to marker changes for every loaded text model. `_updateDecorations` reads up to the new cap and `MarkerDecorations.update` constructs two Sets over the collection, creates a decoration option/range per addition, and calls synchronous `ITextModel.deltaDecorations`, whose implementation inserts interval-tree nodes. The cap is not visibility-aware, so hidden loaded models also retain the extra nodes. The PR's benchmark documents 5,000-marker update medians of 29.01 ms on an M2 and 70.01 ms at 4x slowdown versus 11.34/21.20 ms at the old 500 cap.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the decoration cap at 500 and detect overflow with `take: 501`; the new status warning can still report that existing cap. If raising the cap is required, make it explicitly configurable/opt-in rather than multiplying the default synchronous rendering budget.

Scenarios.Scenario: Publish or republish aggregate diagnostics above the old 500-decoration limit for a large loaded file.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After diagnostics reach `MarkerService`, its microtask event synchronously invokes `MarkerDecorationsService._updateDecorations`; reading, Set diffing, range/option creation, interval-tree insertion, and decoration-change notification must complete on the renderer/UI thread before the editor can finish reflecting the diagnostics. The work is therefore on the visible editor's critical path, and also runs for loaded background models.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and transfer diagnostic batches from the extension host, revive marker fields, and call `MarkerService.changeOne`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing `$changeMany` IPC call per diagnostic collection synchronization; in the PR's realistic six-collection example, six collection `set` operations can produce six IPC calls, each carrying up to the existing 1,000-per-file provider cap. Downstream effective decoration cardinality grows until capped at 5,000.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC calls and payload caps existed, but each resulting loaded-model decoration update read, compared, created, and retained at most 500 marker decorations rather than 5,000.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: IPC delivery precedes the changed synchronous marker decoration update. The PR does not add IPC calls, but it multiplies the UI-thread work performed after each delivered update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Aggregate diagnostics for one loaded resource after provider-level caps and before decoration truncation. The supplied scenario reaches 6,000 from six collections of 1,000; effective processed cardinality is 5,000 plus one overflow probe, not 6,000.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Extension-host diagnostic collection updates arrive through IPC and are handled serially on the main/UI thread. `MicrotaskEmitter` can merge marker resources fired within one main-thread turn, but separate collection IPC messages can each trigger an update; there is no limiter or deferred chunking for decoration creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no decoration cache beyond retained marker identity and the per-model decoration map. On a cold publication, up to 5,000 decorations are created. On warm updates where the first 5,000 marker objects are unchanged, `update` still reads the collection and allocates/scans two Sets of up to 5,000 entries before avoiding `deltaDecorations`; overflow state is coalesced and emits only on threshold transitions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed cap, marker event call path, synchronous interval-tree implementation, and benchmark deltas are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact prevalence of files with more than 500 aggregate diagnostics from several providers is uncertain. The mechanism and cost are not: the supplied reproduction uses six providers, and the PR reports median update time increasing to 29.01 ms normally and 70.01 ms under 4x slowdown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity regression: the default cap increase multiplies synchronous UI-thread work and retained decoration state by up to 10x and measured updates exceed a frame budget. Keeping the prior cap while reading one extra marker preserves the new overflow warning.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch editors/models or toggle validation visibility while the diagnostic-limit warning is active.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Active-editor/model/configuration changes synchronously query the current overflow boolean and may add or remove one language-status item. This constant work is on the editor-switch/configuration path but does not traverse or recreate marker collections.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active editor switches/model switches and validation-visibility configuration changes; marker count does not affect this reporter path after overflow state has been computed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and serialized with active-editor events; there is one lazy reporter per instantiated editor and one active language-status listener. No queue, parallelism, or burst was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The reporter reads overflow state from the existing per-model decoration object in O(1). Its `_limited` field suppresses unchanged notifications, and `LanguageStatusEntry` retains one listener/status disposable for the active editor only.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration is lazy, access is a map lookup, and events are threshold-filtered by both the marker service state and reporter state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; operations are constant-time aside from normal status-service notification fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new status reporter is lazy, bounded, disposed, and performs constant work without new IPC, filesystem, database, network, or subprocess boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or retain multiple text models that already have high aggregate diagnostic counts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model addition synchronously constructs `MarkerDecorations` and calls `_updateDecorations`; opening a model with existing diagnostics must create the decoration nodes before model-add handling completes. For already loaded background models, marker changes perform the same work off the visible editor's immediate paint path but still occupy the shared UI thread.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of loaded models multiplied by effective diagnostics per model, now capped at 5,000 rather than 500.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All model-add and marker-change decoration updates are serialized on the UI thread. A multi-resource marker event loops resources sequentially; there is no concurrency burst or backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Marker and decoration state is retained per loaded text model; reopening reconstructs decorations from the in-memory marker service. There is no visibility-aware cache or lazy creation, so hidden loaded models retain their full capped decoration maps until model removal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the service eagerly creates one `MarkerDecorations` for every `IModelService` model and updates it independently of editor visibility.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously loaded models with several thousand aggregate diagnostics varies by workspace and extension mix, so retained-memory magnitude across a session is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported cap regression: opening latency and retained interval-tree/map state scale up to tenfold per affected model; this is the same causal mechanism, not a separate finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced marker publication, model-decoration updates, editor lifecycle, and language-status reporting. One concrete cap-induced synchronous rendering/memory regression was submitted; the warning/reporting path itself is bounded and introduces no expensive boundary.
